compareCandidate.label: Angle vs. triangle
compareCandidate.description: An angle is two rays sharing an endpoint — an open turn; a triangle closes three segments into a shape that contains three angles.

plainLanguageExplanation: An angle is the amount of turn between two rays that share a start point called the vertex. We measure angles in degrees: a full turn around a point is 360°, so a quarter turn is a right angle of 90°, half a turn is a straight angle of 180°, and a full circle back is 360°. Angles smaller than 90° are acute; larger than 90° but smaller than 180° are obtuse. A protractor measures angles by lining its center at the vertex and reading where the rays point.
whyItMatters: Angles measure turning — the corner of a room, the slope of a ramp, the hands of a clock. They are the hidden numbers inside every shape and the key to navigation and building.
didYouKnow: The word 'degree' for angles comes from the idea of dividing a circle — the Babylonians chose 360 for a full circle, likely because it matches the roughly 360 days in their year.
compareReason: Students confuse the open two-ray angle with the closed three-side triangle — comparing turn vs. enclosed shape makes it clear.
